name: Apollo
tagline: Run permissioned outbound sequences from an uploaded list without supplying contact data

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 900 credits per seat per year granted monthly; trial plans include 50 credits and 5 mobile credits.
tiers.notes: Free plan is also called Starter in FAQ after a trial ends.

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: 30,000 credits per seat per year granted upfront; paid email-provider connections unlocked.
tiers.notes: Official search result exposed $49 billed annually; monthly value from current public pricing.

tiers.name: Professional
tiers.limits: Paid sales-engagement tier; includes broader automation/dialer features, with credit usage governed by Apollo fair-use rules.
tiers.notes: Official crawled page did not expose the full card table; kept public tier price but limited numeric feature claims.

tiers.name: Organization
tiers.limits: Organization tier; minimum 3 users, advanced controls/security/reporting; credit usage governed by Apollo fair-use rules.
tiers.notes: Official crawled page did not expose the full card table; kept public tier price but limited numeric feature claims.

tiers.name: Custom
tiers.limits: Custom enterprise or external-product/data-resale use cases.

pricing.freeTierCaps: $0; 900 credits per seat per year granted monthly; non-paying trial plans include 50 credits and 5 mobile credits.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; cancellations take effect at end of current term; add-on downgrades at end of billing cycle
pricing.hiddenCosts: Add-on credits are recurring, charged immediately without proration, and unused credits expire at end of billing cycle; Unlimited plans have fair-use caps; custom terms required for data resale/external-product use.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Apollo, run permissioned outbound sequences from an uploaded list without supplying contact data. The hard boundary is massive proprietary contact database, enrichment, intent data, and deliverability tooling, plus proprietary data, deliverability, and network effects.
coreLoopDIY: Import a permissioned lead list, personalize a modest outbound sequence, enforce sending limits, and track replies without supplying proprietary contact data.
whatYouLose: massive proprietary contact database, enrichment, intent data, and deliverability tooling
moatNotes: proprietary data, deliverability, and network effects
ongoingBurden: consent records, suppression lists, DNS, bounces, reputation, abuse complaints, provider limits, and changing email rules
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Apollo because the durable value is accurate contact data and deliverability infrastructure; a sequence editor alone is not the product. The recurring cost buys consent records, suppression lists, DNS, bounces, reputation, abuse complaints, provider limits, and changing email rules, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Mautic
priorArt.desc: Open-source marketing automation platform with campaigns, contacts, and email workflows.

alternatives.name: Mautic
alternatives.desc: Import your own list, send a timed SMTP campaign, branch on replies and suppress bounces; enormous machinery for a small sequence.

rejectedAlternatives.name: listmonk
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A fine newsletter sender, but it does not watch replies and stop a sales sequence; wrong kind of email automation.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Basic plan and a small permission-based outreach console DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Apollo in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and a user-chosen transactional email provider; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: import a permissioned lead list, personalize a modest outbound sequence, enforce sending limits, and track replies without supplying proprietary contact data.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Accept CSV imports only after the user confirms lawful collection and records the source.
Provide contact fields, tags, suppression status, consent notes, and a complete change history.
Build a short email sequence with delays, business-hour windows, and per-domain rate limits.
Use the configured provider for sends and process delivery, bounce, complaint, and unsubscribe webhooks.
Stop sequences immediately on reply, bounce, complaint, suppression, or manual pause.
Show deliverability warnings, daily send totals, and a mandatory preview before activation.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out scraping protected platforms.
Deliberately leave out buying or generating personal contact data.
Deliberately leave out automated inbox warm-up networks and evasion of provider limits.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
